Established work supports these controls; the exact benchmark settings are task-specific. Preserve BERT4Rec masked-target training and appended-mask inference ([BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690)). For the objective ablation, hold architecture, initialization, training seed 42, preprocessing seed 0, batches and evaluation cadence fixed. Normalize losses over supervised positions; record actual target counts, updates and GPU-seconds. Equal epochs do not equal supervision when masking changes target counts: distinguish compute-matched comparisons from target-matched comparisons where feasible. Keep the 200-epoch/200-batch ceilings and 43,200 GPU-second aggregate budget, including failures. Preregister checkpoint-selection cadence, stopping and tie rules using validation HR@10; deploy one selected checkpoint/category, without averaging.

Freeze the same 200 users and 99 unique negatives/user/category across comparisons. Report category HR@10 and their unweighted four-category mean. Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog rankings, so conclusions apply to this pinned candidate protocol ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Recommended uncertainty protocol: bootstrap users within each category, resampling identical user indices for both objectives, then recompute the macro difference; report a 95% interval ([paired bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). This measures conditional user-sampling uncertainty, excluding training-seed variability and checkpoint/search-selection uncertainty.

Limit and log adaptive validation queries; preregister hypotheses and selection rules. Repeated validation reuse can overfit, and ordinary bootstrap intervals do not correct winner selection ([Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629)). Leave test labels untouched. Verify deployed-predictor parity by reloading each saved checkpoint in evaluation mode and comparing scores, rankings and HR@10 on identical validation inputs; audit architecture, item mapping, category routing, left padding and final-mask readout ([PyTorch checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models)).
